prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2010 manifesto centres on leaving the European Union to restore sovereignty, save money, cut regulation, and return democratic control to Westminster and local voters. It argues EU membership imposes heavy costs, excessive laws, and legal overreach, and proposes a referendum on EU membership plus wide domestic reforms.

Economy, tax and regulation:
- Raise the personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a 31% flat tax merging income tax and employee NI; phase out employers’ NI over five years; aim to cut the public sector to its 1997 size; abolish inheritance tax when affordable.
- Replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax sending revenues directly to councils; return half of Uniform Business Rates locally.
- Scrap up to 120,000 EU rules affecting business; restore Bank of England prudential control; split retail and investment banking (Glass-Steagall-style); raise bank capital ratios; reinstate lending “corset.”

Jobs, enterprise and skills:
- Create c.1m skilled jobs via long-term programmes: defence procurement, nuclear power (50% of electricity), flood/coastal defences, major transport upgrades, and new prisons using off-site manufacture.
- Establish Production Enterprise Centres; amend takeover rules to protect strategic firms; scrap carbon trading/renewable mandates.
- “Denationalise” universities/FE via student/training vouchers redeemable at independent institutions.

Immigration and asylum:
- Five-year freeze on permanent immigration; long-term cap of 50,000 p.a.; leave the EU to regain border control; time-limited work permits/visas; tripled border staff; no amnesty; deport illegal residents.
- Points-based system after the freeze; repeal the Human Rights Act and leave the ECHR; restore Primary Purpose Rule; end state promotion of multiculturalism.

Law and order:
- Elected County Police Boards; “life means life”; double prison places; three-strikes; boot camps; stronger self-defence rights; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; abolish the CPS.

Defence:
- Increase defence spending by 40%; expand the Army to 125,000 and double the TA; three new aircraft carriers and a larger fleet; more helicopters/transport aircraft; maintain and replace Trident; prioritise NATO; cut MoD bureaucracy.

Health and social care:
- No frontline NHS cuts; elected County Health Boards; scrap SHAs/PCTs; franchise services to public/charitable/private providers on fixed budgets; health vouchers to opt out; restore matrons; free eye tests and dental check-ups.

Education:
- School vouchers; strengthen literacy/numeracy; retain/expand grammar and “professional” schools; more on-the-job teacher training; drop 50% university target; student vouchers; elected Education Boards; franchise schools; reduce Ofsted powers; stronger discipline; support special and home education.

Pensions and welfare:
- Non-means-tested Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week at 65; refocus tax relief on low/middle earners; reinstate dividend tax credit; freeze unfunded public-sector pensions; scrap PPF and NEST.
- Simplify benefits into a Basic Cash Benefit; allow work while retaining support up to the personal allowance; merge child benefits; nursery vouchers; restrict benefits to citizens or residents of 5+ years; workfare for some claimants.

Foreign affairs/trade:
- Leave the EU and seek a Swiss-style FTA; regain a WTO seat; build a Commonwealth Free Trade Area; pursue NAFTA/ASEAN deals; support global democracy.

Energy/environment:
- Climate policy scepticism; expand nuclear to 50% of electricity; support domestic coal; oppose most onshore wind; repeal the Climate Change Act and EU energy directives; set up a Royal Commission; back EVs and rail electrification; invest in flood/coastal defences.

Transport:
- +£3bn/year for roads, bypasses, and three high-speed rail lines; reopen lines; shift freight to rail/canals; oppose Heathrow expansion; support a Thames Estuary hub; “Britdisc” for foreign lorries; fairer fuel duty.

Housing/planning:
- Curb immigration to ease housing demand; use empty homes; scrap regional strategies and the Infrastructure Planning Commission; binding local referenda on major schemes; elected Green Belt conservators; scrap Section 106/social housing quotas in large builds; end empty property rates.

Constitution/governance and culture:
- Direct democracy (binding referenda); AV+ voting; elected Police/Health/Education Boards and mayors; replace devolved legislatures with national MPs sitting part-time; MP recall; abolish regional government; support the monarchy/established church.
- Promote a unifying British culture, protect national brands/imperial measures, support Royal Mail/Post Offices; ban burqa/niqab in specified settings; deport extremist preachers; revive Treason Act; English Parliament; end the Barnett formula; St George’s Day holiday; Commonwealth Day.

Farming and fishing:
- Leave CAP/CFP; maintain farm support during transition; pro-labelling and GM research; relax onerous EU rules; supermarket ombudsman; local reversals of hunting ban; reclaim a 200nm EEZ; end quotas/discards; ban industrial fishing; strengthen fisheries protection.

Other:
- Stronger animal welfare; allow designated pub smoking rooms; reduce burdens on small businesses.
